This work presents a comprehensive music dataset named MusicTM-Dataset that assembles a diverse collection of multimedia data from three modalities: audio, visual, and text. Currently, the dataset includes a set of music videos with synchronized optical flow and descriptive captions obtained from the YouTube-FD dataset. Our goal extends beyond existing research, aiming to explore potential links between multiple modalities within music, as well as the integration of language to decipher intricate musical meanings. We propose a novel task known as multimodal mutual translation, where we seek to adapt an modalities to replicate the content of others, with the aim of improving each other. We develop customized cyclic Generative Adversarial Networks for translating data across different modalities, and conduct experiments using this approach on a music dataset. Our findings indicate that cyclic models yield more natural translations and better preserve the original content compared to conventional generative adversarial networks, leaving room for further optimization and performance improvement. We also establish baseline results for several ancillary tasks, including automatic music video detection, music composition generation, and music sentiment analysis, with the aim of facilitating future research in these areas. Our music dataset is made publicly available, including the implemented models and detailed code for the purposes of facilitating future research.

One major obstacle when utilizing Linked Data lies in developing intuitive and user-friendly interfaces accessible to individuals who aren't technologically inclined. To address this, Ontodia enables diagrammatic data visualization, illustrated in this study with the Wikidata dataset. We've introduced enhancements to a natural language interface that facilitates the exploration and querying of Linked Data entities. By utilizing distributional semantic models to identify and rank entity properties associated with user input in Ontodia, the method demonstrates improved results in enhancing user experience during visual data exploration.

We've discovered that in the nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation with variable refractive index and a defocusing cubic nonlinearity, dark solitons display the same characteristics as in the pure cubic defocusing model. However, adding variable refractive index significantly changes how we assess stability in the dark solitons. Notably, only isolated imaginary axis eigenvalues are found, and energy-based stability is applicable with exponentially weighted Sobolev spaces. Moreover, adding small external influences and confinement still yields spectrally stable solitons in the minimum points. The system's solitons persist as small waves travel through it, and we take this behavior into account when investigating the overall stability of dark solitons.

This collaborative approach in visual analytics aims to facilitate seamless interaction between humans and machines, according to various established frameworks. To bridge the gap between theoretical foundations and practical implementation, we introduce an intuitive model for system-assisted guidance and a corresponding library. We present a model for system-supplied guidance based on predefined templates and derived methods. Furthermore, we create the Lotse library, allowing developers to specify guidance strategies using definition files and automatically generate functional code. The Lotse library offers an innovative approach by providing reusable guidance strategies for easily retrofitting existing applications with guidance and promoting the development of generic guidance pattern templates. Through case studies involving VA researchers with different levels of expertise, we demonstrate the library's effectiveness and efficiency in creating guidance. Moreover, we analyze our framework's cognitive properties to evaluate its flexibility and outline potential research avenues to harmonize guidance practice with its underlying complex theory.

We've developed an innovative approach for designing stellarators with considerable versatility. Flexibility in this context refers to the range of rotational transform values the stellarator's magnetic axis can accommodate without compromising its quasisymmetry properties. Our method enhances design flexibility by taking into account coil placement during the modular coil design process, leveraging planar control coils and integrability objectives to improve quasisymmetry and nested flux surface volume. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by optimizing a coil set inspired by NCSX design, which not only achieves a range of rotational transform targets but also surpasses the NCSX design in nested flux surface volume. Our research reveals that stellarator design is characterized by a fundamental tradeoff between flexibility, quasisymmetry, and nested flux surface volume.

Achieving uniform temperature distribution within catalytic fixed bed reactors is critical for both optimal production yield and operational stability.  However, obtaining precise temperature readings simultaneously with good spatial and temporal resolution in these systems remains difficult. Our research utilizes the capabilities of real-time MRI imaging in conjunction with the temperature-dependent shift in water's proton resonance frequency to obtain in situ temperature measurements in a cylindrical fixed bed reactor. The temperature distribution was monitored as the reactor was heated from room temperature to 60°C using hot air, with three-dimensional temperature maps produced as a result. The findings show significant temperature variations along both axial and radial dimensions, corroborated by optical temperature probe measurements, with an average error of 1.5°C. The presented MRI thermometry technique presents new avenues for the in-depth study of mass and heat transfer in gas-solid fixed beds, potentially being adapted for further applications in reactive gas-solid systems in the future.

Within a cellular environment, proteins and nucleic acids autonomously separate, resulting in the spontaneous formation of membraneless droplets. This process underlies the development of numerous sub-cellular compartments. In a model system designed to understand condensate self-assembly, interactions between a large number of different molecular species were studied and programmed to test for variability and accuracy. The number of different droplets formed from mixtures was found to be limited, and through computational simulations, it was demonstrated that droplet composition is highly dependent on specific interactions and droplet size. Furthermore, it was discovered that small droplets are formed first and then grow through the accumulation of more molecules, and these findings are supported by previously obtained data.

Using the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager on the Solar Dynamics Observatory, we studied how a major leading sunspot rotated in NOAA AR 11429 during two powerful solar flares. A notable sunspot rotated in an unconventional direction, influenced significantly by the solar eruptions. Moving disturbances within other sunspots, caused by the solar flares, traveled rapidly and altered the magnetic properties associated with the sunspots in question, providing valuable insights into the dynamic process governing the sunspots' development.

This note presents a new category of map functions known as oriented colored broken submersions, which forms the most basic type of map functions that adhere to the b-principle, and is nearly equivalent to the set of oriented submersions in 2 dimensions. It demonstrates that the Madsen-Weiss theorem, which can be viewed as a variation of the standard Mumford Conjecture, is derivable from a specific application of the b-principle to oriented colored broken submersions, combined with the findings from Harer's stability theorem and Miller and Morita's work.

This research involves comparing the efficiency of Balancing Domain Decomposition by Constraints (BDDC) and Algebraic Multigrid (AMG) methods on various cardiac mechanics problems. By incorporating an algebraic coupling algorithm, the BDDC method can easily handle diverse problem formulations and configurations. Nonetheless, a major drawback of the BDDC method is that it often necessitates an off-the-shelf solver for the coarse problem. Although flexible, the AMG method faces challenges in handling irregular subdomain shapes and inconsistent mesh sizes, and its performance is often unsatisfactory for cardiac mechanics problems. A key asset of the AMG method is that it usually doesn't require a coarse solver. This research aims to evaluate the performance of both methods on a range of cardiac mechanics problems with diverse parameters and problem setups. The experimental findings indicate that the BDDC method consistently demonstrates superior convergence compared to the AMG method.

The ever-growing influence of user-generated content is significantly altering the digital landscape, driven in part by the proliferation of systems supporting content creation, sharing, and management. Among these systems are tag-based platforms that enable users to collaborate in annotating shared items such as images and URLs, leading to user-generated metadata pools and collaborative behavior. To unlock this potential, a comprehensive understanding of current systems is required, which involves characterizing these systems based on usage patterns, the evolution of user-generated content over time, and the underlying social dynamics.

Recently, proposed bianisotropic acoustic metagratings offer promising possibilities for passive acoustic wave manipulation, notably in flat acoustic lenses and ultra-high frequency ultrasound imaging. This concept, however, has not yet been implemented at the MHz frequencies common in ultrasound imaging due to difficulties in fabricating complex microstructures. Advances in two-photon polymerization now enable precise manufacture of sub-wavelength structures in this range. However, shrinking structures in size introduces another challenge, where increased thermoviscous effects lead to considerable energy losses, which need to be factored into the design. This work introduces three novel microacoustic metagrating designs capable of refracting normally incident waves by approximately 35 degrees at 2 MHz, utilizing shape optimization techniques and the linearized Navier-Stokes equations. Using two-photon polymerization, we fabricated and experimentally validated microscopic acoustic metamaterials, successfully redirecting incident waves and supposing that with further refinements, these elements could be integrated into integrated, high-resolution ultrasound imaging systems.

This paper primarily focuses on the long-term behavior of strong solutions to the two-dimensional compressible FENE dumbbell model. Utilizing the Fourier splitting technique, we demonstrate that the $L^2$ decay rate is given by $\ln^{-l}(e+t)$, with any positive integer $l$. Through the application of the time-weighted energy method, we manage to enhance this rate to $(1+t)^{-\frac{1}{4}}$. Under the condition that the frequencies are sufficiently low, by incorporating the principles of the Littlewood-Paley theory, we find that the solutions have properties belonging to certain Besov spaces of negative order and establish the most favorable $L^2$ decay rate.

Implementing integrated access and backhaul (IAB) through wireless connections offers a promising way to develop flexible and high-density networks. Mobile IAB, which utilizes millimeter wave (mmWave) technology, is especially notable for its versatility in 5G networks. However, mmWave IAB faces challenges related to signal strength, directly proportional to the distance between the base station and devices. This distance issue can render some areas unreachable, limiting network accessibility and backhaul capacity. This study introduces a new online backhaul allocation method that maximizes network accessibility and backhaul capacity. The proposed algorithm assigns IAB bands to base stations in a way that prioritizes those farthest away, leveraging a modified rang-based fair allocation (RFA) strategy. Compared to alternative scenarios, our method shows substantial improvements in both accessibility and backhaul capacity.

In this study, we conduct an extensive examination of five leading global optimization algorithms as a hyperparameter configuration problem to understand the overall impact of their settings on performance. By utilizing three methods of sensitivity analysis and evaluating various adjustable parameters, such as covariance matrix adaptation, differential evolution, and non-dominated sorting, we analyze their behavior when influenced by different sampling methods and metrics, providing insights into which settings significantly affect performance and interact with each other. The ranking of influential parameters suggests an optimal order of tuning, and our results also shed light on the overall stability of the algorithms.

The paper addresses misconceptions surrounding Jefimenko's equations, which are derived from Maxwell's equations, for a specific charge and current configuration obeying the continuity equation. It subsequently derives a non-radiative condition across inertial frames, consistent with the stability requirements of an atom, and establishes that this condition is analogous to certain relationships between charge, current, and the wave equations. The paper then demonstrates that these relationships lead to quantised electromagnetic field energy displaying the characteristics of the Balmer series.

Despite notable breakthroughs in reinforcement learning, numerous significant hurdles remain when applying it to dynamic and ever-changing problems common in critical domains, including robotics and complex gameplay. Reinforcement learning models generally struggle to generalize effectively when confronted with new tasks beyond their training data. In response to this challenge, the field is seeing an increased focus on continual learning methods, and to accommodate this shift, new evaluation frameworks are being developed, including ones that emphasize the importance of robust performance in unexpected situations. In response to the lack of these types of evaluation platforms, we have created a continuous learning environment centered around a chess-like game called Lepton, where agents can be trained and tested for their ability to adapt to novel information and scenarios. Given the level of strategy and random elements integrated into the game, it serves as an ideal medium to test cutting-edge continual learning methods and to investigate fundamental questions regarding the type of challenges these models face and how effective they are in handling unexpected situations.

Liger, a next-generation infrared device at the W. M. Keck Observatory, will be paired with the Keck All-sky Precision Adaptive-optics system to optimize performance. By covering the wavelength range from 0.81 micrometers to 2.45 micrometers, Liger combines multiple observing modes, offering various spatial scales and fields of view. However, Liger's data complexity necessitates a customized data processing system to refine its output in real-time, making it compatible with science-oriented data presentation tools. This processing system, called the Data Reduction System, will be responsible for delivering refined data to astronomers and uploading it to the Keck Observatory Archive. We have established a prototype of this data processing system and defined the communication interface with the relevant software systems at the observatory.

This study uncovers a broad class of non-trivial and smooth travelling waves that arise in the vicinity of the Couette flow in 2D Euler equation, at low regularity in vorticity $H^s$ for $s<3/2$. The velocity of these waves is directly proportional to their distance from the Couette flow. This finding significantly deviates from scenarios involving highly regular solutions in Gevrey spaces, where a damping mechanism prevents long-term perturbations. This research is particularly notable given that it contrasts with previous results showing no non-trivial travelling waves in areas immediately surrounding Couette flow with regularity higher than $3/2$.

We experimentally control the linear polarization of exciton-polariton condensates using optical traps with elliptical geometries that favor specific polarization modes. Due to anisotropic splitting in the cavity, ground state degeneracy is lifted, yielding fine structure modes along the trap's axis and orthogonal to it. These modes are selectively occupied by the condensate. Our results reveal a unique method for polarization control with potential applications in spin-based photonics and research on complex optical systems with adjustable coupling properties.

This study's primary objective is to provide evidence and disproofs for the deterministic Kardar-Parisi-Zhang type equations including non-local gradient elements. The specific focus lies within a particular class of nonlocal problems formulated within a given domain in higher dimensions. The formulation is based on an equation where the fractional Laplacian of a variable $u$ is equal to the sum of a nonlinear term that involves the norm of the variable's gradient and an additional parameter with an applied force function. The conditions of existence and non-existence are explored with varying coefficients in a specific mathematical framework and solutions to related problems from earlier works are provided.

The  COVID-19 pandemic, triggered by SARS-CoV-2 in 2020, was officially classified as a global health crisis by the WHO. As a result, the world is relying heavily on public health precautions such as social distancing measures to curb the virus spread and maintain the healthcare system functionality. With the isolation of communities, access to reliable information has become restricted. Consequently, the health minister in South Africa updates the public every day on COVID-19 infections, including affected individuals' demographic and travel details. Meanwhile, the National Institute for Communicable Diseases provides daily updates on testing numbers, case counts, and fatality rates via infographics but often fails to release patients' ages or other critical transmission details. Recognizing the need to effectively share this information, the University of Pretoria's Data Science for Social Impact research team developed an open-access data platform comprising a data warehouse and an online dashboard, enabling transparent and efficient data sharing. This endeavour revealed challenges pertaining to data availability, credibility, and governance in the public sphere within South Africa. This research aims to address these concerns by presenting the successful implementation of a public-facing data platform as a model solution to the existing data-related problems.

Freiman's 3k-4 theorem generally posits that if subsets A and B, of size k and comprised of integers, share a sumset with a size near 2k, then A and B exhibit considerable similarity to arithmetic progressions. In this paper, we aim to enhance this by limiting the number of possible summands available from subset B. It's shown that if subsets A and B, of size k, meet the criterion that for every four-element subset of B, the sumset A plus that subset doesn't exceed 2k, it follows that A and B exhibit considerable similarity to arithmetic progressions.

In medical contexts, diverse information often arises from various sources, which when combined enables healthcare professionals to form more precise opinions. For retinal analysis in particular, recent advancements have led to increased use of multiple imaging methods: standard two-dimensional fundus photographs and more detailed three-dimensional imaging techniques such as optical coherence tomography (OCT). Our study demonstrates the value of integrating data from these various sources - 2D retinal photographs and 3D OCT scans - in constructing a comprehensive model for retinal lesion detection and classification. By integrating information from all dimensions, our method achieves improved performance over other methods that focus solely on 2D or 3D data. Specifically, our approach delivers classification accuracy of better than 90% for both benign and severe macular edema, and also identifies the precise location and extent of the edema within the retinas. Our research indicates that integrating information from diverse medical sources offers a promising strategy for enhancing diagnostic accuracy and flexibility in retinal analysis tasks.

X-ray images contain subtle characteristics with predictive information about patients who are likely to experience severe COVID-19 symptoms.  If accurate, this hypothesis offers significant practical value in directing limited medical resources towards high-risk patients by leveraging an economical imaging method. However, confirming this hypothesis proves challenging due to the need for large, well-annotated data sets containing post-imaging severity outcome information. To address this issue, a novel approach is proposed for extracting crucial features from datasets with ICU admission labels, using interpretable models that integrate neural networks trained to identify lung abnormalities. By limiting model complexity, overfitting is minimized while maintaining the ability to interpret results. Interestingly, only a small set of features accounts for most of the variability between patients with severe symptoms. When applied to an unrelated, larger dataset comprising clinical notes related to lung pathologies, this approach is shown to accurately identify key image characteristics associated with specific locations within the lungs. Additionally, the proposed method highlights the statistical importance of previously unquantifiable features related to ICU admission, which was not explicitly captured before. Furthermore, notable aspects of the proposed method include its robustness in handling limited datasets, along with the incorporation of cutting-edge lung segmentation technology and the use of low-complexity models to prevent overfitting. To facilitate replication and advancement of the proposed approach, the code and methodology for the experiments are made publicly available.

We analyze the transmission eigenvalue problem involving $u$ and $v$ in the Sobolev space $H^1(\Omega)$ associated with $(\Omega, \sigma, \mathbf{n}^2)$. Considering the case where $\Omega$ is a 2 or 3-dimensional ball, and the functions $\sigma$ and $\mathbf{n}$ only depend on the radial distance $r$, we find a sequence of transmission eigenfunctions that tend to concentrate their energies around the boundary of $\Omega$ as the associated wavenumbers $k$ increase without bound. If $\sigma$ and $\mathbf{n}$ are constant, we prove the existence of transmission eigenfunctions that become localized around the boundary of $\Omega$. Our results generalize the recent studies in the mentioned literature and also illustrate the influence of medium parameters $\sigma$ and $\mathbf{n}$ on the geometric patterns of transmission eigenfunctions via numerical experiments.

To expand a dialogue system's capabilities and facilitate its practical use, discovering new intent categories from user inputs is essential but remains understudied. Building on prior research, which typically relies on supervised approaches with labeled data, this work investigates how to leverage large, unlabeled conversation data and limited annotated data to identify new intent categories. Specifically, it investigates whether there are any unsupervised changes in user behavior corresponding to new intent categories and uses supervised learning to predict these changes. The investigation is conducted using two publicly available datasets: EMOSD and SEMEION, and a part-of-speech tag-based unsupervised approach to new intent discovery is presented. The study demonstrates the efficacy of this approach, which outperforms baseline methods, and reveals that unsupervised intent discovery is more effective than supervised learning in some cases. The methods and findings are expected to guide the development of new intent discovery approaches.

The classical universal bundle functor W mapping from the category of simplicial groups in C to the category of simplicial sets in C lifts to a monadic structure on the category of simplicial groups in C, and this extension holds for simplicial algebras defined by any Lawvere theory that includes group theory.
In our analysis, we demonstrate that a finite group of order $r$ possesses no more than $$7.3722\cdot r^{\frac{\log_2r}{4}+1.5315}$$ subgroups.

This study re-examines the Adler-Bobenko-Suris H2 equation. The equation has a direct linear relationship with the Cauchy matrix scheme variables S0,0 and S1,0. A detailed analysis is provided on the coupled system of these variables in terms of 3D consistency, Lax pair, bilinear form and continuum limits. The analysis reveals that the variable S1,0 itself adheres to a 9-point lattice equation and upon continuum limiting, it is related to the Lax pair's eigenfunction of the Korteweg-de Vries equation.

This paper delves into the source of high false positive rates in Visual Relationship Detection (VRD). During training, we discovered that the relationship proposal distribution is skewed, with the majority of incorrect relationships being proposed simultaneously. To address this issue, we present a novel method called Balanced Distribution Proposal (BDP), which aims to evenly distribute relationship proposal probabilities across all categories. By doing so, BDP decreases the false positive rate significantly. Furthermore, BDP's mechanism results in more accurate support boxes for object detection, thereby enhancing the overall performance of the VRD system. Experimental outcomes for both VRD and object detection tasks demonstrate BDP's effectiveness, yielding improved performance in terms of F1-score for VRD and accuracy for object detection.

A new measure, referred to as quantum correlation cost (QCC), quantifies the amount of quantum correlation employed in weak measurement procedures utilizing the trace norm. It's demonstrated that the QCC is directly linked to the trace-norm-based quantum discord (TQD) by a factor dependent on weak measurement strength. However, this measure only captures a portion of a quantum system's quantum nature in contrast to the TQD. Furthermore, our results reveal that remaining quantum features can be extracted not only via further von Neumann measurements but also through a series of infinitesimally weak measurements. We exemplify these outcomes using a Bell-diagonal state.

Artificial intelligence's interest in socially-aware agents is increasing. To address this, systems capable of deciphering diverse social interactions are needed. Understanding social situations requires not only recognizing individual actions but also grasping relationships among individuals. To tackle this challenge, we introduce Social Relationship Graph, a novel approach that leverages knowledge about social relationships to accurately identify visible relationships among characters in a scene. By fusing this information with action predictions, a deep learning model seamlessly integrates multi-objective optimization for simultaneous action and relationship prediction. Thorough testing on Diversely-annotated Charades and ActivityNet datasets demonstrates the superiority of our model. It outperforms state-of-the-art methods in predicting character relationships and exhibits improved performance in simultaneous action and relationship prediction.

Capturing long-range relationships in scene understanding tasks is a crucial goal in computer vision. While CNNs excel in many vision tasks, they have limitations in modelling global, structured relationships due to their localized nature. A fully connected graph like the self-attention mechanism in Transformers is beneficial, but comes with prohibitively high computational costs. We propose a new graph neural network called dynamic graph message passing network that efficiently models long-range relationships by adaptively selecting relevant nodes in the graph for message passing, thereby reducing computational complexity compared to prior approaches. This allows us to design a self-attention module and a new Transformer-based backbone that outperforms state-of-the-art models in image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation, while using significantly fewer resources and parameters. The code and models will be publicly available.

Optimized hardware is often required in embedded systems, leading to a common operation called multiple constant folding (MCF), where large constants are computed within a system to free up hardware resources. This technique relies on executing constants in a vertical or horizontal sequence before storing the results, which usually involves multiplying operations. To address the lack of a comprehensive base number for MCF optimizations, this paper provides a thorough analysis, starting with identifying the most efficient base numbers for various factorization methods. It proposes a dynamic base number selection approach, which chooses the optimal base number based on the costs of several factorization methods. To achieve this, the paper develops a linear time algorithm to identify the worst possible factors for any given number. This approach yields optimal base numbers that are simpler and more efficient than previously known methods. Furthermore, the paper investigates various accumulator architectures and suggests a dynamic base number scheme that takes into account the specific characteristics of each accumulator type. Experimental results demonstrate the significant improvement in area, energy consumption, and delay for eight standard accumulators, ranging from 48% to 100% better than the previous best known methods.

The intersection of quantum computing and deep neural networks has recently given rise to a growing research field, known as quantum deep learning. Despite previously being separate entities, advancements have revealed that quantum circuits share parallels with artificial neural networks, paving the way for widespread adoption. This paper delves into the foundational aspects and core principles of quantum deep learning, highlighting key breakthroughs along the way. It also explores the challenges inherent in quantum deep learning research from multiple viewpoints, followed by a discussion of prospective future directions and practical applications.

The radio frequency (RF) accelerator technology continues to be fundamental in 
high-energy physics (HEP) experiments, where significant progress has been 
made over the past decade in advancing the field. This progress could soon lead 
to upgraded existing facilities, enhancements to facilities still under 
construction (such as PIP-II), well-established proposals, or newly emerging 
ideas like the FCC-ee and future proton intensity upgrade at Fermilab, among 
others. Innovations in RF technology not only contribute to HEP but also extend 
beyond to fields such as nuclear physics, basic energy sciences, and other areas, 
as evidenced by European XFEL, LCLS-II and related facilities, or SHINE, 
EIC, and FRIB. Therefore, an extensive R&D program focusing on RF technology 
is needed to tackle challenges in accelerator-based applications and introduce 
new, promising technologies.

In the near future, physicists anticipate that the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) will discover new physics. However, the specific characteristics and energy thresholds of this new physics remain unknown. It's probable that insights gleaned from LHC data will require supplementary information obtained from a lepton collider to conduct a thorough investigation. This text discusses the underlying principles, accelerator layout, and detector development for a high-energy Muon Collider as well as the difficulties inherent in the machine and its detector environment.

We have determined the dispersion relations for relativistic fluid modes in various configurations - scalar, vector, and tensor - and found the differences between their behavior in divergence-based and relaxation-time-approximation models. Our comparison also shows correspondence with first-order causal theories and highlights how a specific divergence-based model can predict damped tensor waves. This aligns with kinetic theory's results. It's interesting that both hydrodynamic and holographic fluids display similar properties. These findings reinforce the feasibility of using hydrodynamics to analyze the interaction between gravitational waves and fluids.

Our research assesses whether the cosmic background of Hawking radiation from primordial black holes could be the source behind the observed excess radiowave signals. By assuming that dark matter exists entirely as these black holes, we calculated that temperatures in the range of 0.1 to 1 K would be sufficient to explain the anomalies. This requires an extremely large number of primordial black holes, with approximately one per cubic meter of space, which is similar to the estimate for their density as a potential component of dark matter. We then determined the radio frequency brightness temperature produced by these black holes, which ranges from very low values at 0.1 kHz to nearly 300 Kelvin at 100 kHz. This is a result of the unique spectral characteristics of Hawking radiation, which transitions from a thermal spectrum to a wave train-like distribution as the black hole mass decreases. Ultimately, we conclude that while the idea of primordial black holes is compelling, the data does not support the theory that dark matter consists of these black holes, which is also validated by constraints from nearby star light curve observations.

Introducing the Virtual Secure Platform (VSP), a pioneering solution that brings together multi-opcode general-purpose sequential processing with Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) to enable Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC) at a secure computing offloading level, such as cloud computing. The VSP safeguardingly shields both input data and function evaluations against adversaries in a secure computing offloading scenario like cloud computing. To enhance performance, our innovative VSP architecture features a five-stage pipeline design that increases circuit evaluation parallelism. Moreover, a custom-designed Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) was created to decrease processor gate count, accompanied by comprehensive toolchains allowing for arbitrary C program compilation into our custom ISA. To further boost performance, CMUX Memory-based ROM and RAM implementations over FHE were developed. Experimentation results confirm the effectiveness of the pipelined architecture and CMUX Memory approach in significantly accelerating VSP processing speed. We made the VSP source code available and achieved remarkable results, with each instruction taking under 1 second to complete, a substantial improvement over current existing processors over FHE. The VSP prototype has outperformed the best competing processor, executing nearly 1,600 times faster.

Researchers investigate polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTAS) for solving specific constraint satisfaction problems, such as Maximum Independent Set or Minimum Vertex Cover on graph classes that have limited connectivity.

A previously developed approach by Baker achieved PTAS on various graph classes including planar graphs. Further, Romero, Wrochna, and Zivny developed a simpler PTAS for certain graph classes using the Sherali-Adams LP relaxation for maximum CSPs with constraints defined by arbitrary non-negative functions.

This research is extended to CSPs with constraints that have multiple possible values. The only restriction for such constraints is that they must contain an element that is at least as acceptable as all other elements.

A new PTAS is presented that relaxes constraints to linear programs, assuming certain conditions are met. It is demonstrated that this technique cannot be generally applied to CSPs with arbitrary non-negative functions, as previously suggested by Bubbolo, Molinaro, and Zivny.

The new algorithm works by first reducing the problem to a smaller instance with constrained subintegral region in the hypercube. The algorithm then uses a search procedure to find a satisfactory solution within that region, utilizing LP-duality to determine the bounds of the acceptable region.

Additionally, the methods presented can be used to develop PTAS for maximum CSPs with constraints that have multiple possible values, as long as they contain an element that is at least as acceptable as all other elements. This includes developing PTAS for any graph class that has O(2

Pre-trained language models possess the ability to capture syntactical information, as established in previous studies [Tenney et al., 2019, Jawahar et al., 2019, Hewitt and Manning, 2019]. This work presents two unsupervised constituent parsing models, UPOA and its enhanced version UPIO, both of which use the syntactic distance from self-attention weight matrices in pre-trained language models to evaluate sentence structures. Further experiments demonstrate the significance of linear projection matrices in self-attention for accurate parsing. Consequently, the unsupervised models were transformed into few-shot parsing models, FPOA and FPIO, to learn better parsing matrices with limited annotated trees. On the Penn Treebank dataset, the unsupervised model UPIO achieved parsing accuracy comparable to that of a trained unsupervised model on BERT [Devlin et al., 2019], while the few-shot parsing model FPIO surpassed its supervised counterpart FPION on the English dataset and another model, the English parser developed by Kwiatkowski et al. [2020], in both two- and three-way annotations scenarios.

High-definition hyperspectral images possess the unique capability to distinguish between diverse objects within intricate environments by analyzing each pixel across various frequency ranges. Although HSI cameras are becoming increasingly accessible, associated algorithms have not been extensively utilized. This research delves into a novel application, specifically employing hyperspectral images for cityscape object segmentation using an unsupervised learning approach that circumvents the need for manual object classification. This method capitalizes on the rich spectral data inherent in HSI images, which facilitates efficient object segmentation within complex urban environments. By analyzing the inherent properties of HSI images and developing a corresponding segmentation framework, we demonstrate how these images can improve low-quality labels, ultimately leading to higher accuracy in object segmentation. Our results demonstrate that this technique produces competitive results and outperforms manually refined labels in certain scenarios. Moreover, the refined labels derived from HSI images contribute significantly to the enhancement of object segmentation. This research validates the significant potential of HSI images in advanced visual applications, showcasing the benefits of integrating spectral data and semantic analysis for enhanced visual task performance.

This study reveals intriguing evidence of a complex internal rotation pattern within a less massive and less luminous star that has evolved into a giant. Typically, lower and intermediate mass stars retain their rapid rotation rates during their main sequence phase. However, once these stars expand into giants, we expect a faster core rotation rate compared to their outer layers. Contrary to these expectations, KIC 9267654's rotation speed is observed to be higher near its surface rather than at its core, which presents a challenge to angular momentum conservation principles. To validate our findings, we updated the constraints based on spectroscopic surface measurements, verified that the detected oscillation patterns align with the previously determined core and outer layer rotation rates, and confirmed that the star exhibits no significant chemical abnormalities. Additionally, we eliminated the possibility of a starburst that might have impacted rotation rates. Ultimately, we were unable to explain the observed inversion of rotation rates, which presents an enigma, and we consider possible solutions, including the influence of a star-in-star event, interaction with a nearby star, or a core composed mostly of helium, with rapid core rotation, which still needs theoretical validation.

In algorithmic literature, the underlying computation model is typically implicit and assumed to be based on the RAM model. Despite being widely adopted, the RAM model lacks a solid theoretical foundation, characterized by inconsistent definitions and a lack of cohesive results. This research aims to rectify this issue by developing a new RAM model with desirable algorithmic properties and robust complexity classes, particularly linear-time computability for problems like LIN and CONST-DELAY-lin. The proposed computation model employs a suitable combination of integer and boolean arithmetic operations, with novel insights into their computational powers, along with a comprehensive study of fundamental properties and a comprehensive study of fundamental operations. Additionally, the RAM model's potential applications in algorithm design is also explored, along with a discussion of existing algorithms and potential new developments.

To tackle the data sparsity problem affecting session-based recommendation models that predict the next item users will choose, researchers combined self-supervised learning with reinforcement learning. They proposed a new session-based recommendation framework that uses a novel encoder-decoder network to generate diverse, ordered item lists. By removing important input during the decoding process, the model is forced to retain item representations and sequence information, effectively creating a self-supervised task. As a result, the model is able to leverage reinforcement learning to refine its output. Unlike previous methods, the proposed model does not rely on external labels but instead optimizes its performance using session-level feedback. Due to its ability to handle sequences, the model is able to recommend items that are not only similar to the user's historical behavior but also varied and relevant. Evaluations using public datasets demonstrated the model's superiority over existing state-of-the-art approaches, showcasing its ability to balance diversity and relevance.

This research presents a novel method for generating LCD codes using group rings, resulting in LCD codes that have zero unicharacter subsets. A new theorem is developed to achieve this, which provides guidelines for creating these LCD codes. By employing this method, we compute LCD codes for various prime fields, achieving the highest known dimension for a given cardinality in some cases. Our approach also enables the construction of semi-DLCM codes, which are a variant of LCD codes, by utilizing group algebras instead of group rings. This method produces strong LCD codes, including optimal and near-optimal codes, such as a $[504, 252, 251]$ code in this study.

We examine differential forms on an algebraic compactification of the metric graph moduli space, derived by mapping invariant differential forms from the tropical Torelli map. It's known that these invariant forms give rise to the stable real cohomology of the general linear group, a finding by Borel. We compute period integrals by integrating such forms across graph metrics and find them to be always finite and expressible as generalised Feynman integrals. Our integrals have further application in identifying non-zero homology classes in the graph complex, providing novel perspectives on the cohomology structure and forging links between graph theory, motivic Galois groups and quantum field theory.

In various object categorization tasks, particularly in visually complex conditions, it has been demonstrated that recurrent neural networks (RNNs) can outperform feedforward models.  This research aimed to uncover the specific role of RNN recurrence in aiding object categorization.  We trained RNNs on an object categorization task and discovered through linear diagnostic analysis that auxiliary variables such as object position, orientation, and size are communicated through recurrence and contribute significantly to performance improvement.  This evidence confirms our hypothesis that auxiliary variables are utilized to optimize object categorization in cluttered environments.

Despite numerous studies on non-Hermitian topology, the influence of correlations remains a significant unresolved issue. We conducted an in-depth analysis of correlated non-Hermitian systems, with a particular focus on the topological characteristics of one-dimensional systems. Our results reveal that correlations cause a significant reduction in the topological classification from $\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ for one-dimensional systems with a single synthetic dimension, along with $\mathrm{U(1)}$ symmetry and point-like exceptions. We also investigated the properties of extended non-Hermitian topological states and found that correlations systematically destroy the chiral and charge of the system. Consequently, the system undergoes a topological transition to a trivial phase. Furthermore, the observed disorder-induced transition can be quantitatively described within a minimal model, where the correlation effects are concentrated in a finite segment of the synthetic dimension. The minimal model enables us to derive a topological invariant, thereby providing a comprehensive understanding of the system. The correlation-driven destruction of the non-Hermitian topological effect possesses a universal character, unaffected by the specific nature and length of the synthetic dimension. Nevertheless, the system exhibits a wide range of distinct phases across diverse disorder strengths.

Recently, Golay complementary matrices have gained popularity due to their utility in omnidirectional precoding techniques. This research extends Golay complementary matrices to higher-dimensional spaces known as multi-dimensional Golay complementary arrays and presents novel construction methods for pairs and quadruples of GCA. A set of ring identities is introduced to facilitate these constructions. Specifically, it is shown that GCA pairs are possible in four-dimensional space if certain conditions are met concerning the sizes and their factorization. Additionally, in binary GCM quadruples, possible sizes are postulated as unlimited, which is confirmed for sizes 78x78 and a few scattered instances, but the exact determinability of this set remains uncertain.

Research on Higgs boson production is conducted, combining CMS data from 13 TeV LHC and previously collected data from 7 and 8 TeV LHC, totaling 104.6 fb^-1. The findings from four-lepton final state analysis provide joint constraints on Higgs boson width and its interaction with electroweak vector bosons. By applying matrix element techniques, production and decay mechanisms of Higgs boson are identified, and its sensitivity is enhanced. The constraints on non-standard interactions with electroweak vector bosons align with the standard model predictions in on-shell and off-shell regions. Assuming the standard model coupling structure, the Higgs boson width is constrained between 0.4 and 5.4 MeV, while the simulated expected range is between -8 and 20 MeV. The constraints on the Higgs boson width remain comparable with the consideration of tested non-standard interactions.

Incorporating dimensionality reduction techniques, researchers address the complexities of analyzing numerous spectral bands within bi-temporal hyperspectral images. This study proposes a cutting-edge approach using a novel deep convolutional autoencoder that fuses features across hierarchical levels and receptive fields. By utilizing an unsupervised change detection technique, it overcomes the limitations of other label-dependent methods. By integrating various techniques to extract changes from the images, it significantly outperformed current state-of-the-art methods in unsupervised change detection across diverse datasets.

Consider the set $\mathcal{S}$ of squares and let $\mathcal{W}$ be a subset of natural numbers such that when you combine these two sets with addition, the result encompasses all natural numbers greater than or equal to some finite number $N_0$. Now, the $\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{S},\mathcal{W}}(n)$ denotes the count of all possible pairs of $s$ from $\mathcal{S}$ and $w$ from $\mathcal{W}$ whose sum is equal to $n$. Previous studies, such as those by Chen and Fang, have shown that the total count of these pairs minus the total natural numbers up to $N$ exceeds $N^{1/4}$ multiplied by the natural logarithm of $N$. Here, a refined version of that finding is provided with a revised lower bound of $N^{1/3}$.

Quantum tunneling is a primary mechanism by which phosphorus dopants in silicon retain thermal energy and interact with each other. This paper predicts that the presence of a neighboring hole can slow down the tunneling motion of a phosphorus dopant by a notable amount, and causes the wave function of the dopant to extend further than normally anticipated. This peculiar behavior is due to the attractive force between the dopant and the bound hole, which is strong enough to affect tunnel rates. This hole-dopant interaction is hoped to aid researchers in identifying and studying individual phosphorus atoms within devices made of silicon. This level of detail is anticipated to be crucial in distinguishing between coherent and incoherent effects on quantum interactions and processes.

Several disciplines have been influenced by optimization techniques in various real-world scenarios, hence their importance is being increasingly acknowledged by the community. As a result of this growing interest, researchers have been able to develop multiple open-source frameworks for optimization, ultimately contributing to innovation in both techniques and their practical applications. In the context of this study, we introduce a novel framework, known as LibOPT, for efficiently implementing and prototyping nature-inspired optimization algorithms. By integrating 15 established techniques and 112 benchmark functions, as well as supporting 11 novel hypercomplex-based approaches, our framework surpasses others in its domain, thus marking it as a groundbreaking innovation in optimization software development. Utilizing LibOPT under the C paradigm proves to be remarkably user-friendly and adaptable, as evidenced by the inclusion of clear source-code examples demonstrating the practical usage of benchmark functions.

Given an algebraic variety X that has a transitive action from the group Aut(X), the highest degree of transitivity of this action is called the transitivity degree. This degree is denoted by the maximum value of m for which Aut(X) acts transitively m times on X. In cases where Aut(X) is m-transitive for any positive value of m, we define the transitivity degree to be infinite. This study involves determining the transitivity degree for specific varieties, such as quasi-affine toric varieties, and homogeneous spaces, while exploring related open problems and conjectures.

In non-commutative space-time deformations, the definition of identical particles breaks down. These models are described by non-abelian space symmetries represented by a four-momentum group. Our approach recognizes that for multi-particle states, the total system momentum is the only well-defined property. Calculating the total momentum involves non-commutative composition of individual particle momenta, which become ambiguous. Our results indicate that previous Fock space constructions were flawed due to incorrect assumptions and lack success. We demonstrate that momentum exchange underlies a relativistic covariance principle in the braiding of quantum numbers, solving a persistent challenge in the field.

We apply the two-photon absorption transient current technique to study
properties of wide bandgap semiconductors. We utilize this technique to
investigate charge transport in scCVD diamond by exciting its charge carriers
with a femtosecond laser. Due to its two-photon nature, the technique confines
charge carrier generation in 3-D around the laser focal point. This localized
charge injection enables us to study the semiconductor bulk with high 3-D
resolution. We mapped the diamond's bulk electrical field at varying depths by
taking advantage of charge spatial confinement. The results were then compared
to X-ray diffraction topography. The approach allows for unique insights into
spatial charge transport variations in transparent wide bandgap materials.

Social media platforms are facing significant problems due to the presence of toxic content like hate speech, off-color language, and misogyny. These difficulties have caught the attention of the Natural Language Processing (NLP) community, driving innovative research in the field. In this study, we report on the performance of our models in the inaugural Arabic Misogyny Identification challenge, where we evaluate three models that can learn multiple tasks simultaneously, alongside their individual-task counterparts. Our approach relies on the pre-trained MARBERT language model to analyze text inputs. Our results indicate that the proposed models achieved top-tier outcomes, securing first, second, and third place in both the misogyny identification and classification tasks.

This study centres around the solvability of a distinct class of fractional backward stochastic differential equations that take into account past influences within their generators, under Lipschitz condition it's demonstrated that the existence and uniqueness of such equations are assured. Furthermore, a key comparison theorem has been formulated.

We examine if controllers obtained using model-based Reinforcement Learning, which employs an environment model to find the optimal policy, remain robust and adaptable when dealing with slight environmental variations. Building upon the concept from PILCO, a method for probabilistic policy search, our research demonstrates that constraining the uncertainty in the Gaussian Process model's dynamics has a beneficial effect on policy updates and results in more resilient controllers. In addition, our findings highlight the practical advantages of this approach in a simulation-based evaluation.

Several key network communication challenges such as caching and computation are interconnected. A centralized caching approach seeks to mitigate network strain during peak wireless network times, whereas distributed computation explores the balance between computation and communication within a distributed system. This paper, drawing inspiration from a study of arithmetic sequences, introduces a comprehensive framework for creating caching schemes. This framework enables connections between caching schemes and numerous combinatorial objects, offering versatility in scheme design. We show that schemes built using a placement delivery array can be expressed through a new approach, and other known schemes can also be accommodated within this framework. Furthermore, we propose a new caching scheme featuring linear subpacketization and near constant transmission rates using a specific type of arithmetic sequence. Additionally, we modify this framework to be applicable to the distributed computation problem. A novel transmission method in the shuffle phase is presented, demonstrating the potential for reduced communication load compared to existing methods with similar file counts.

We establish a formalization of the Scott model in univalent type theory, adopting a constructive and predicative framework. To capture the essence of non-terminating processes in PCF, we employ the lifting monad, which serves as a fundamental concept. Our formulation employs basic axioms for the Scott model and demonstrates that the lifting monad can be derived from these axioms, similar to how it arises from the category of presheaves in category theory. Additionally, we show that monadic natural transformations between predicative universe constructs can be derived from the axioms, which in turn allows us to formally prove key properties and theorems of the Scott model, while also maintaining constructive validity.

Hanzer and Muić's work on degenerate Eisenstein series cancellations has been built upon, 
extending their method and outcome to a specific set of Eisenstein series, 
specifically those formed from the combinations of two fixed representations 
$\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ within $GL_2(F)$. 
These cancellations are correctly interpreted within the context of automorphic representations, 
and we offer partial solutions to two related conjectures proposed by Soudry.

Designing effective collision avoidance systems for mobile robots remains a key challenge, particularly when accounting for the robot's spatial structure.
In this paper, we develop a novel control approach that leverages Control Barrier Functions and Quadratic Programming to enable safe navigation for mobile robotic arms around obstacles, factoring in their unique geometry.
Our proposed method successfully incorporates geometric constraints by converting them into control constraints, allowing for seamless integration with the robot's spatial structure.
Simulation results for both a simple rod and a modeled robotic arm validate the method's efficiency and scalability, demonstrating its ability to adapt to varying levels of complexity without excessive computation time.

Natural language processing, a crucial field of study, strives to comprehend text via digital analysis, despite the inherent imperfections arising from diverse forms of written and spoken language. This work delves into employing various graph-based methodologies for resolving the challenge of text summarization via a selective extraction technique. Two key indicators – sentence overlap and edit distance – are employed for gauging sentence similarity.

Researchers have suggested the application of quantum interferometry and information processing in Bose-Einstein condensates. However, the current understanding of BECs relies on complex descriptions, often through quantum field theory or nonlinear differential equations. These descriptions sometimes conflict with key principles in interferometry and information processing. Nevertheless, a possibility of compatibility remains, and we provide a solid foundation for quantum operations, derived from solving evolution equations, and build upon this base with control techniques and efficient state sampling methods to develop practical nonlinear gates, especially a nonlinear Hadamard gate. Furthermore, our work in BEC interferometry and quantum computing redefines the paradigm by incorporating principles from nonlinear quantum mechanics, effectively applying it to interferometry and information processing.

This paper aims to accomplish two distinct objectives. Firstly, it seeks to establish a unicity theorem for meromorphic mappings from a complete Kähler manifold to a complex projective space, under the constraint of limited intersection with hypersurfaces. Secondly, the paper aims to prove a unicity theorem for the case of nondegenerate meromorphic mappings that share a specified number of hyperplanes in a particular geometric configuration.

Polynomial system solving plays a crucial role in various applications to capture nonlinear geometric attributes. To obtain a solution, various algorithms convert the system into an equivalent bilinear form, focusing on eliminating variables from a given equation to analyze nondegenerate instances. This process usually involves a parameterized elimination step, but the resulting expression often lacks clarity and is computationally complex. This study introduces a new algorithm, Clarhaf, specifically tailored for systems with a nondegenerate locus that is both sparse and low-dimensional. By leveraging these characteristics, Clarhaf efficiently computes a simplified and easily interpretable parameterized form of the system, facilitating the deployment of established decoding and localization techniques from coding theory.

Direct photons have been measured at $p_T<5$ GeV/$c$ for midrapidity and most central events of Cu$+$Cu collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}=200$ GeV. By calculating the $e^{+}e^{-}$ excess in the $e^{+}e^{-}$ mass distribution over hadronic contributions, we found that quasi-real direct virtual photons significantly contribute to the photon spectrum. In Cu$+$Cu collisions, photons show a clear increase above a binary-scaled $p$$+$$p$ fit, and their transverse momentum spectra follow a similar trend as Au$+$Au collisions, involving a similar number of participants. We have determined the inverse slopes of the photon excess spectra at $285\pm53$(stat)$\pm57$(syst) MeV/$c$ and $333\pm72$(stat)$\pm45$(syst) MeV/$c$ for minimum bias and most central events, respectively. Moreover, we found that the photon rapidity density in Cu$+$Cu demonstrates a similar power-law behavior versus charged particle multiplicity observed in Au$+$Au collisions at the same energy.

The Turan tetrahedron problem seeks to calculate the Turan density of the tetrahedron graph K4^3 by finding the maximum l1-norm of a K4^3-free n-vertex 3-uniform hypergraph's codegree vector. We develop a new method for determining hypergraph extremality and apply it to calculate the asymptotic extremal function of K4^3, yielding an upper bound that is asymptotically equal to (1+1/2\omega^2) (1+1/2\omega^3) n, where \omega is the plerichromatic number. We also determine the codegree squared sum of an extremal K4^3-free hypergraph and demonstrate that one of the extremizing hypergraphs achieves the upper bound for all n, including those not divisible by 4. Furthermore, we determine the asymptotic extremal function for the hypergraph K4^2 \square K2 and prove a conjecture proposed by Allen about the tetrahedron problem. Our results demonstrate that extremal projective Turan problems may possess extremal projections with a constant codegree vector, and in such cases, the asymptotic extremal function can be computed as a linear combination of codegree weighted random walks. We utilize the distributed version of the Szemeredi-Erdos extremal Combinatorics Theorem to evaluate such sums and leverage a generalized version of the Erdos-Stewart characterisation of minimal

Achieving a seamless visual experience and optimal system performance when displaying line joins on vector maps requires an efficient anti-aliasing technique. However, the limitations of OpenGL API hinder optimal rendering results when approximating the anti-aliased effect through multiple triangles. In an attempt to rectify this issue, this study introduces a straightforward yet high-performance algorithm utilizing two triangles to replicate fan-shaped line joins via alpha operation. Our findings indicate this technique yields a genuine anti-aliasing effect while reducing memory consumption, raising frame rates, and preventing overlap rendering in map visualization. Our novel anti-aliasing method has been applied in notable applications such as Tencent Mobile Maps and Tencent Automotive Maps.

The multivariate interpolation operator is traditionally constructed using piecewise linear functions to approximate absolute differences between values. In this study, we develop a novel, transcendental interpolation function derived from the hyperbolic tangent, providing more precise approximations of functions that increase linearly with the distance. Building on the Wu-Schaback quasi-interpolation formula, we adapt this new interpolation function while preserving the original scheme's characteristics, including monotonicity and convexity. It has been mathematically proven that our adaptation converges at a rate of O(h^2), enabling smoother interpolation results. Several numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the method's efficiency and accuracy.

Pulsar halos are large-scale, high-energy emission structures, formed when energetic electrons and positrons break free from pulsar wind nebulae. As a novel category of gamma-ray emitters, pulsar halos serve as optimal probes for examining the diffusion of cosmic rays within the Galaxy's localized areas, as well as their escape from pulsar wind nebulae. Research on pulsar halos has brought to light that their associated diffusion coefficient is substantially lower than the overall average in the Galaxy, thus generating considerable interest among scientists. We delve into the recent breakthroughs in the study of pulsar halos, including the distinct properties of these sources, identified pulsar halos, theoretical mechanisms underlying their exceptionally slow diffusion, their pivotal roles in investigating cosmic-ray propagation and particle injection, and the implications on the puzzles of excess positrons and the widespread TeV gamma-ray excess. Lastly, we outline the prospective research avenues based on the anticipation of discovering more pulsar halos and carrying out deeper investigations into the brightest sources.

Transportation systems are frequently hindered by unpredictable weather conditions.
Current methods of weather prediction, using either a network of sensors or a vehicle-mounted camera, are limited in scope and costly.
A robust weather detection system is crucial for seamless operation of transportation services in diverse weather conditions.
However, this task is complex due to the varied nature of weather and the scarcity of distinct characteristics that distinguish different weather conditions.
Existing approaches to this problem are largely confined to specific environments and only tackle the classification of two weather types.
In this study, we introduce the RFS dataset, which includes images representing three categories of weather (rain, snow, and fog), and propose a novel algorithm utilizing super-pixel masks for data augmentation to yield satisfactory results using multiple Convolutional Neural Network configurations.

Our analysis examines how climate change interest shifts among diverse groups and how their individual interests interconnect. Initially, we track the individual trends, followed by developing a cross-influence model that we then validate using a VAR model. Our results indicate significant fluctuations in the general public's climate change interest, as evident from our creation of a Climate Change Index for Europe and the US based on media mentions, whereas economists show relatively little interest as measured by prominent journal publications. Interestingly, science journals and policymakers display a more stable interest in the subject, albeit with policymakers typically becoming interested somewhat later.

Soft grippers are increasingly popular across various applications due to their versatility and flexibility, yet accurately modeling them to manipulate virtual objects is challenging. To address this, researchers have employed different physics-based rendering techniques but often require substantial domain knowledge. In response, a novel, easy-to-implement soft gripper model been developed from an empirical and practical standpoint. This model uses a novel multi-stage deformation process, taking into account the compression, bending, and expansion of soft materials. Additionally, a simple and reliable method for calculating the mass of a soft gripper has been proposed. To demonstrate its efficacy, the new model was integrated with a physics-based simulator of grasping and manipulation tasks, and successful results were achieved in a variety of experimental conditions. Furthermore, a novel enhancement to particle simulation was introduced to address the soft gripper's compression, replacing the traditional use of a mesh. This method is suitable for real-time physics-based rendering and has promising implications for VR and interactive computer graphics.

The success of the Gradient Descent method is largely due to its simplicity and broad applicability, but it struggles with suboptimal local minima and slow convergence, making it inefficient after many iterations. To address these limitations, a multi-agent Gradient Descent algorithm was developed, which distributes the optimization task among multiple agents. Since each agent's progress is independent, the risk of getting stuck in suboptimal local minima is significantly reduced. Additionally, as there are multiple agents, the algorithm can terminate successfully even if some agents find suboptimal minima. Meanwhile, the rate of convergence accelerates due to shared knowledge, allowing for early termination of unnecessary iterations. Moreover, as the number of agents increases, the algorithm's efficiency improves further. To further improve performance, a clean-path policy was implemented, which disables the optimization process for underperforming agents, preventing them from causing distractions with suboptimal solutions. Consequently, the clean-path policy boosts the algorithm's robustness and reliability by ensuring that most agents focus on the global minimum, significantly improving its overall performance.

High-energy emissions from ancient supermassive black holes can provide a direct look into the black hole activity in the early universe. Specifically, misaligned jets of high-redshift active galaxies should make up a significant portion of these distant galaxy populations. This study uses a highly detailed analysis of data collected from multiple observations of a particularly old and distant galaxy called J2102+6015. High-resolution imaging of J2102+6015's energy emissions, which were captured through a highly precise technique called VLBI at a wavelength of 8.4 GHz, revealed two distinct energy-producing regions. This imaging revealed two distinct energy-producing regions aligned east to west, approximately 1/3 of a milliarcsecond apart. Our calculations suggest that J2102+6015 is very likely a younger, dense structure rather than a quasar or a highly radio-emitting galaxy. This is due to, among other things, observations suggesting a lack of gas surrounding the energy-producing region. Our analysis also suggests that J2102+6015 is very likely a massive black hole with a mass of 10^9 solar masses. This is based on observations of its energy output, as well as measurements of its movement. Our findings also indicate that J2102+6015 is very likely in the early stages of a highly radio-emitting galaxy (GRB) period. This is observed in the shape of its energy-producing region, which is found to be symmetric in the eastern and western directions. Our calculations

This research focuses on improving survival time prediction for lung cancer patients, which, despite significant progress in recent years, still lacks effective solutions. Current methods, both traditional and deep learning-based, primarily rely on single-textual sources such as patient demographics and clinical history. Unlike existing approaches, this study explores the potential of combining multiple data types like text-based clinical information and visual medical scans to inform survival time predictions, simulating the decision-making process of a medical professional. Building on this insight, this work introduces the Lite-ProSENet model, which integrates multiple data modalities and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, yielding an unprecedented 89.3% concordance in predictive accuracy using a dataset from 422 non-small cell lung cancer patients.

A well-designed state representation is crucial in the learning process of Reinforcement Learning. Natural language can be utilized in numerous tasks to either represent the state or constitute it entirely. This overview focuses on the techniques employed by researchers to create natural language state representations, underscoring the need for more transparent and contextualized models, thorough justification of design choices and assessments of the relative effectiveness of varying methodologies.

A novel approach combining machine learning is introduced, enabling the accurate reconstruction of high-redshift cosmological density perturbations through observed quasar spectra analysis. By leveraging sophisticated simulations of cosmic structure formation, a substantial synthetic dataset of absorption spectra and associated 1D matter densities is generated. With this dataset, a series of machine learning models are constructed to predict matter density power spectra. We achieve reconstruction accuracy of approximately 1% for certain wavelengths while noting a corresponding error increase at higher wavelengths. Furthermore, we investigate the size of datasets required to attain a specified error rate, highlighting the data requirements for a desired level of accuracy. This work lays the groundwork for analyzing the forthcoming large-scale datasets anticipated with future observational facilities.

This paper examines certain types of non-weight modules connected to Lie algebras of the Weyl type. Firstly, we establish the characteristics of modules whose restrictions to $U(\frak h)$ are one-dimensional over Lie algebras representing differential operators on a circle. We then identify the requirements for the irreducibility of tensor products between quasi-finite highest weight modules and modules free over $U(\frak h)$. Additionally, we show that these tensor products are isomorphic only if their corresponding base modules are equivalent, before expanding our findings to cover general Lie algebras representing differential operators.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them and their rivals.
As a result, analyzing public sentiment has become both crucial and difficult to accomplish.
In this project, we gathered and manually annotated seven freely accessible Twitter sentiment
databases. We then compiled a new set of training and testing data from these sources. An
LSTM-based classification model was developed to determine the sentiment expressed in
individual tweets. The model's performance was assessed using the newly created dataset.

Recent advances in open-domain dialogue models have achieved significant breakthroughs.
Despite this, developing a scalable chat system poses a major challenge due to
the requirement for substantial human-human dialogue data to support features
like persona, style, or safety. To tackle this issue, our work aims to introduce
role constraints to open-domain dialogue systems that enable them to consistently
maintain assigned roles during human conversations. Achieving this involves
defining a role specification with specific criteria for stated features and
policies on allowed types of utterances. To build this system efficiently, we
propose a framework for collecting data that leverages few-shot learning from
large language models, thereby enabling the creation of role-compliant dialogue
datasets from scratch. Furthermore, we examine various open-domain dialogue
system architectures in terms of their ability to meet role specifications and
maintain natural conversation. Results from both automatic and human evaluations
reveal that our models perform satisfactorily in terms of role conformance, while
still delivering competitive performance on overall conversational metrics.

The binary black hole merger's aftermath leaves a lasting mark on space-time known as gravitational wave memory, and multiple events create a background of residual disturbance known as the stochastic gravitational wave memory background (SGWMB). Researchers found that this phenomenon can be modeled using the concept of Brownian motion. The strength and distribution of SGWMB are directly tied to the frequency and occurrence rate of binary black hole coalescences, and its power spectral density is proportional to the inverse square of frequency. Unlike the more common gravitational wave background produced by binary black holes, SGWMB's characteristics allow for distinct signals from different astrophysical events to overlap and combine, potentially holding clues for better understanding the events that created them. By comparing these signals, researchers might be able to determine which event occurred first. The calculation of SGWMB assumes that all gravitational wave memory signals add up equally, but further research is needed to determine if this assumption holds true. The concept of SGWMB provides a novel approach to studying the events of binary black hole coalescences, and its application could be expansive, including using gravitational wave memory signals from other celestial events to learn more about their occurrences.

A hypothetical supersymmetry framework offers an explanation for why large particles weren't discovered by the Large Hadron Collider; this framework predicts the universe underwent a phase transition around the time of the universe's birth that may create ripples in space time that scientists could detect. Developing a realistic model based on how this supersymmetry is broken, researchers found this phase transition can lead to masses in certain heavy particles that may create more particles and a new theory of neutrino mass, as well as ripples in space time that may signal the universe's birth. The same model can help predict signs of these early ripples in space time that may signal the universe's birth. The universe's phase transition can potentially create tiny, extremely dense regions known as black holes that date back to the universe's birth.

A reliable and efficient communication system known as semantic communication aims to reduce data transfer and ensure seamless connectivity to diverse users and services. A novel approach to this challenge is presented, incorporating an emergent signaling game framework with a neuro-symbolic artificial intelligence system that facilitates causal reasoning. To design a context-specific communication language, an alternating maximization algorithm optimizes utility values between communication nodes. This language enhances the vocabulary for message transmission by splitting complex data into simpler components and allows for generalization to unforeseen scenarios. A neural network model is used to reconstruct causal states based on the relevant data attributes at the transmitter, which are then evaluated by a receiver that implements a symbolic logical formula execution using AI components. Specifically, this implementation leverages the Generative Flow Networks tool for improved reliability and efficient training. This causal state reconstruction is further augmented with a uncertainty quantification module, informing the receiver about the reliability of the reconstructed state. Experimental findings demonstrate that this novel semantic communication system surpasses traditional methods in data recovery, exceeds human-level generalization capabilities, and effectively manages uncertainty at the receiver end.
